scenario: [LERR.1.4.12]: a pair the operation evaluates and then ends before it completes records nothing. The NOT node and the trapping join read one schema, so one B is both the blocker and the candidate. With `a1` live, asserting `b1` with `b1.k == a1.k` and `y = 0` offers the pair `((a1), b1)` to the join `c.x / c.y > 1.0`, which traps (an all-Int division [LEXP.7.15.1]); but the NOT node blocks `(a1)` in the same assert, so the pair is not live when the propagation completes, and no ComputationError is recorded. The order the two nodes are right-activated in does not matter: deepest first evaluates the pair and then ends it, shallowest first never evaluates it (formal witness `lerr_1_4_12__transient_pair_records_nothing`, formal/idris/Rete/NetworkTraps.idr). PATH: libds holds the trap from join_tests_pass (rete/beta.c hold_match_trap) and drops it at the end of the event because the token has left the join's left memory (ds_rete_beta_flush_match_traps); Mercury drops it in ds.match.lerr_1_4_12_derived. The runtime differential runs the same program (113_transient_trap). `r` does not fire.
rules_ds:
schema A scope logical:
    k: String key

schema B scope logical:
    k: String key
    x: Int mutable
    y: Int mutable

rule r:
    A a
    no B b where b.k == a.k
    B c where c.x / c.y > 1.0
->
    log info "r fired"
